recommended_steps.detail: Size the budget and measure latency and memory on a real corpus and host before a consuming service turns acceleration on by default.
recommended_steps.title: Measure before making acceleration a default

see_for_yourself.expected: The opt-in, the route fields, the refusal codes and the three monitoring scopes
steps: Open project/ADOPTION.md at 'Opt in to exact vector acceleration and monitor memory'
see_for_yourself.title: Read the monitoring guide

what_just_landed.detail: A long-lived consumer can pass one VectorAcceleration to bound single-shelf or stack search; shelves whose index opted into Palace 0.7.0's vector change feed are searched from memory with the same answer as the exhaustive search, and each result reports how every shelf was served.
what_just_landed.title: Opt-in exact vector acceleration

what_just_landed.detail: vector_status reports a shelf's stored vectors from its feed state, stats reports the cache's budget, owned bytes, headroom, counters and resident rows, and the process's peak resident memory comes from the operating system. Unknown figures are reported as unknown, never zero.
what_just_landed.title: Memory and pressure monitoring at three scopes

what_just_landed.detail: Only operational unavailability can fall back, and only when the consumer chose fallback; divergence, malformed feed state, other cache failures and authorization refusals fail with their own codes.
what_just_landed.title: Fail-closed refusals
